Harrismith Water Heroes

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Last year Carte Blanche exposed the complete collapse of the Harrismith Municipality or Maluti-A- Phofung due to political corruption. Its been under administration for the last two years and the citizens of Harrismith are desperate, they regularly don’t have water or electricity or refuse removal due to lack of maintenance or funds for chemicals or spare parts to maintain the water supply. Businesses are closing down and residents are leaving because of the shocking state of disrepair and unemployment is on the rise. At the beginning of 2019 a group of Harrismith residents from across town got together and stepped in to try and take back control of basic services. It began with the town’s water supply. Known as the Harrismith Water heroes they describe themselves as a non-political non- racial organization.

Summary:
Petrus Claasen Van Eeden a local farmer who knows about irrigation systems first replaced the main pump for the towns water supply at his own expense and then proceeded to repair a number of broken and leaking pipes assisted by volunteers from the community. Then they began unblocking sewers and buying spares. Over the next year they identified major water leaks and repaired them , in one incident saving 286 000 litres of purified water that was just left to run back into the river which originated at the Municipal officers and they knew about for 9 months but did nothing about. They restored water to the town’s reservoir and bought chemicals to purify the water to the tune of R4.4 million, half of this has been recouped from COGDA .
On Thursday and Fridays they remove the rubbish from the town, including the townships and suburbs using private vehicles, paying 15 staff to collect the rubbish and paying for the petrol themselves. Now the residents have bought tar and are beginning to fix the potholes themselves.


Further information:
At the beginning of December, 95% of Harrismth was without power and so they hired private contractors to repair and replace transformers and missing cables and ring-fenced lines. When Eskom began load shedding instead of load shedding in stages across town the Municipality just shut down the whole town down so when they switched on again it blew the entire system because of lack of maintenance.
Some local businesses have negotiated to pay Eskom directly to keep their factories going but farmers and businesses supplied through the Municipal grid were stranded. The impact on farmers and business has been massive. I have footage of farm workers having to offload 32 tons of soya for feed production by hand. Local Petrol stations spent R120 000 on diesel to keep generators running. People lost the food in their deep freezes which they had bought with their end of year bonuses.
Harrismith Water heroes is privately funded, they do get donations form the residents and local government - COGTA have repaid them half of the money spent to date. Their big debate now is how to proceed, can residents stop paying their rates and pay the Water Heroes directly for the services they deliver? They have documented the process and have videos illustrating all the repairs and negotiations.



Extra Budget Items:
Additional car for Liz to go and shoot and recce but Liz will cover her own accommodation in lew of the 2nd vehicle hire. Two night of accommodation for cameraman

Script:


Link: What do you do when your town is falling apart, the taps have run dry, here is sewerage running in the streets and the electricity grid is blown, call ghost busters, no The Harrismith Water heroes
Script: It all began a year ago, the town of Harrismith had been without water for 40 days and for the residents of Intabazwe it had been months. The youth were about to shutdown the N3. Community leader Sam Twala had had enough and went to find the source of the problem, here met local farmer Petrus Claassen van Eeden who had the same idea
Petrus I know the pumps and pumping because of irrigation farmer. So I went to the pump station. It's just on the hill there, Nuwejaar Spruit pump station. And I arrived there and then Sam was also there that and we became friends after that. But I looked at the pump and I realized that it was really easy to fix.
Script: Returning with Sam to Intabazwe, Petrus attended a community meeting with the Municipality
Sam “I am at the forefront to say to the youth, look, burning tires, barricading roads won't solve the problem. Let's go and see and fix”
Petrus “I asked the municipality if there was enough authority in this meeting to give me the responsibility to fix the water. And then and that's actually how we started
Sam You know, we stood up. Within four days. We managed to have water. Look, this is not a joke. We said together we can make it. And the whole year, Harrismith was like this.
Script: Petrus bought and replaced the pump, but they soon realised the entire water system was severely neglected. It took 3 months to repair the line starting with cleaning the filtration plant, and paying for chemicals to purify the water. At times it was really dangerous work.
Petrus And there's a lot of the foot soldiers, the people on the ground that still work for the municipality that come to help us. And we had really had fun. It was it was really nice. I was just buying the fittings to fix the leaks. And because they had no support, there was not nobody. They couldn't buy fittings
Derek So, I mean, the whole community got involved with most of it,
Petrus No, it was from from the ground up. Everybody really got involved. It was it was quite an amazing time. I mean, the management of the Municipality that came later. I don't think they realized that we were really left on our own then, they forget that
Script: Harrismith is part of the Maluti-a-Phofung Municipality- MAP which has collapsed under political corruption, looting and mismanagement.
Link: MAP was placed under administration more than two years ago when the debt to ESKOM was more than R2.7 billion rand now that amount has almost doubled while things have gone from bad to worse
Script: 13 Businesses won a court settlement to pay Eskom directly, keeping the lights on for Maluti- a- Phofung, but by 2019 it was completely bankrupt. ESKOM seized all the assets and the Municipal officers collapsed. There was no billing for 8 months, no refuse collection, and sewers burst. Vice chair of the water heroes Willy Tshabala says they started to reclaim their town.
Willy It's better because you start to say communities must take responsibility remember that their constitution only gives people who are elected and people who are employed to look after the property that belongs to the community. This infrastructure then belongs to us as a community. It does not belong to government. It does not belong to maluti a Phfung
Sam We just volunteers that want to bring the dignity of the town back. Non politically non racially You see. And I'm surprised president once said let everyone in his town stand up and do something. It's exactly what we are doing
Script: This morning they’re heading out to repair a burst pipe which had been neglected for a month
Derek So have you got the technical expertise?
Willem We get technical expertise in none of us are technically inclined as far as this is concerned. But do we consult people as we need?
Script: Once they started they couldn’t stop, from doing major infrastructure repairs to cleaning the abandoned Harrismith Municipal office. Anyone who had a skill was brought on board. Former plumber Christopher Radebe led the team repairing over 400 leaking toilets and clearing blocked sewers.
Derek Sam problem he had was water wasn't reaching these houses higher up because of the pressure. and you’ve install this- water heroes.
Sam Water heroes because people can't wait for the trucks they don’t even know when they are coming you see
Script: Hlengiwe Motaung says they have been without piped water since 2015
Derek Question about water heroes 01:56.
“We have faith in them. Because since they provided us with tanks that has helped a great deal.
Script: Diverting another service delivery protest, the water heroes restored power to residents who had been without electricity for two weeks
Petrus There was a there was a riot starting and the people wanted to actually blockade the N5. And we walked in there and there was a there was the guy was so angry, he was crying. I told him that the best thing we can do now is that they must please help us to carry this cable over the highway and we can put it through the highway when we did that.
Script” December load shedding hit Harrismith businesses hard, the grid for 12 days because like the rest of town, there had been no maintenance for years. Contractors struggled to restore power without transport or tools depending on locals to assist them. Petrol station owner Emile De Beer says the lack of services is crippling
Emile “If you've got a business that that's burning 60 thousand rand a month in diesel just to generate to power and all, you've got a fast food business and you don't have water…..So
Derek You have invested a lot of money.
Emile Yes, we have, and we want to employ a lot of people. That's 50 new jobs that's created in the MAP area. But we are very in need of water to run this warehouse and to run this ice factory.. And this for four months, there has been no water
Script: We went to visit the new administrator, appointed last year in August by the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs because the Recovery Plan was failing.
Up sound Derek-Not much here
Script: Administrator Blake Lefatola freely admits that things are in a bad state
Blake Look, I'm saying that there is some progress that we are making, but it is not at the pace that we would want it to happen. I think the point that we need to make that we accept accepted is that because of the state of disrepair, we don't have the money immediately to make a change in the next month or two.
Script: And although he welcomes the support of business and the community, he is trying to restore order.
Blade “When the mess actually happened, Water Heroes did certain things, which under normal circumstances is not permissible. [03:39:26] when we assumed office, we made it very, very clear that no one is entitled to work on municipal infrastructure if you are not a municipal employee. We have had instances of where, the water heroes actually came into municipal premises, took a truck To perform particular functions without being authorized,
Script: But the water heroes say they stepped up in a time of crisis, and the former Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, Minister Mkhize agreed to reimburse Petrus who had carried the financial load
Link: As with most aspects of life it all boils down to money or the lack of it the water heroes claimed over R5 million rand and it’s the outstanding balance of R2.8 million that is under dispute
Blade “No, no, no. I think that they are being disingenuous. Why do you sit down with me? You negotiate with me and say, you know what? I'm still being owed money.
Derek Basically saying that he or the municipality and the previous administration never agreed to pay five million. That's the basis of it.
Willy “They've never agreed to paid anything, by the way, because the municipality at that particular time, it has collapsed. Eskom took everything that office at Maluti a Pfukeng at Qwa Qwa it was empty Therefore, this community. Then we took the initiative to fix what was wrong.
Blade “ We don't have any beef with you guys. But if I come out to be a service provider, turn yourself into a company and subject yourself to the rules of the game.
Derek “ The administrators says that going forward, you must tender for work and you must maybe form a corporation.
Willy “ If the municipality is back on its feet, then the Municipality must do their work we are not here for business. That is why we have never even charged them for any extra work money from what Mr Claasen did
Script: “Some residents have lost faith in the recovery plan and are calling for a boycott of rates. Richard Moore of Mountainview Dairy suffered major losses over December and if it were not for the water heroes he would still be tankering in water.
Richard “ We can't afford to carry the debt that this municipality has created. So we need to formalize a separate rate payers
Emile “We think everybody is ready to pay their money to a ratepayers association so that we know we are not buying 50 BMW is and paying 50 councillors salary every month before we change the light bulb in our streets
Blake “You are obliged to take care of your municipal rates and service charges on a monthly basis, if you are getting any service,
Derek “ they say they're not getting any service whatsoever. So why should they pay?
Blake “They woke up this morning with electricity, even, although we have got water challenges people are getting water with tankering through to them
Script: There are no simple answers here. The Water Heroes say they responded to the president’s message of thuma mina" send me, and they not going to stop.
Willy “ We'll carry on with our work as long as the community of Harrismith will then pay the money.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Last year Carte Blanche exposed the complete collapse of the Harrismith Municipality or Maluti-A- Phofung due to political corruption. Its been under administration for the last two years and the citizens of Harrismith are desperate, they regularly don’t have water or electricity or refuse removal due to lack of maintenance or funds for chemicals or spare parts to maintain the water supply. Businesses are closing down and residents are leaving because of the shocking state of disrepair and unemployment is on the rise. At the beginning of 2019 a group of Harrismith residents from across town got together and stepped in to try and take back control of basic services. It began with the town’s water supply. Known as the Harrismith Water heroes they describe themselves as a non-political non- racial organization.
metadata.Summary: Petrus Claasen Van Eeden a local farmer who knows about irrigation systems first replaced the main pump for the towns water supply at his own expense and then proceeded to repair a number of broken and leaking pipes assisted by volunteers from the community. Then they began unblocking sewers and buying spares. Over the next year they identified major water leaks and repaired them , in one incident saving 286 000 litres of purified water that was just left to run back into the river which originated at the Municipal officers and they knew about for 9 months but did nothing about. They restored water to the town’s reservoir and bought chemicals to purify the water to the tune of R4.4 million, half of this has been recouped from COGDA . On Thursday and Fridays they remove the rubbish from the town, including the townships and suburbs using private vehicles, paying 15 staff to collect the rubbish and paying for the petrol themselves. Now the residents have bought tar and are beginning to fix the potholes themselves.
metadata.Further information: At the beginning of December, 95% of Harrismth was without power and so they hired private contractors to repair and replace transformers and missing cables and ring-fenced lines. When Eskom began load shedding instead of load shedding in stages across town the Municipality just shut down the whole town down so when they switched on again it blew the entire system because of lack of maintenance. Some local businesses have negotiated to pay Eskom directly to keep their factories going but farmers and businesses supplied through the Municipal grid were stranded. The impact on farmers and business has been massive. I have footage of farm workers having to offload 32 tons of soya for feed production by hand. Local Petrol stations spent R120 000 on diesel to keep generators running. People lost the food in their deep freezes which they had bought with their end of year bonuses. Harrismith Water heroes is privately funded, they do get donations form the residents and local government - COGTA have repaid them half of the money spent to date. Their big debate now is how to proceed, can residents stop paying their rates and pay the Water Heroes directly for the services they deliver? They have documented the process and have videos illustrating all the repairs and negotiations.
